item.title: CISA adds Puppet Enterprise and Core vulnerability CVE-2026-115731 to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have updated Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog directives under Binding Operational Directive 22-01, enforcing emergency remediation mandates for an actively exploited endpoint configuration server flaw. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit memory handling logic errors to manipulate server data and push unauthorized code across managed endpoint fleets.
The emergency security directive covers Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core vulnerability CVE-2026-115731 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8. The vulnerability affects Puppet Enterprise versions 2023.8.0 through 2023.8.12, 2025.0.0 through 2025.12.0, and 2026.0.0, as well as Puppet Core 8.x and 9.x releases. Unauthenticated remote threat actors transmit crafted requests to Puppet central servers, bypassing confidentiality controls, altering node configuration files, and executing arbitrary code. CISA mandated a December 1 compliance deadline for federal civilian agencies to deploy updated maintenance builds.
Subverting central infrastructure configuration servers introduces catastrophic supply-chain risks across corporate IT environments. Because Puppet servers automate policy enforcement, software distribution, and access management for thousands of endpoints, an unauthenticated compromise of the central Puppet master permits threat actors to deploy malicious scripts and gain full control over connected enterprise hosts.
- Upgrade Puppet Enterprise installations immediately to fixed release versions 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1, or 2026.0.1. - Update Puppet Core agent and server packages to builds 8.22.2 or 9.1.3 across all managed Linux and Windows hosts. - Restrict network access to Puppet master administrative ports, isolating configuration servers behind out-of-band VLANs. - Audit Puppet manifest run logs for unauthorized policy modifications, unscheduled script deployments, or anomalous agent registrations.
Infrastructure automation defense demands immediate patch deployment and rigid network access controls to ensure central configuration management servers remain protected against remote code execution exploits. #CodeDefence #Puppet #CVE2026115731 #CISA #KEV #DevOps #SysAdmin #AppSec #PatchManagement #SupplyChain

item.title: Active exploitation targets Cisco Expressway vulnerability CVE-2026-76466 following public PoC release
item.description:
Perimeter security advisories published today warn of active cyberattacks targeting enterprise collaboration gateways. Remote threat actors actively weaponize improper input handling routines to compromise clustered gateway appliances and prepare tooling for internal lateral movement.
The security bulletin covers Cisco Expressway Series devices affected by vulnerability CVE-2026-76466 carrying a CVSS score of 9.6. Following the public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit script, threat telemetry confirms adversaries are actively targeting exposed Cisco Expressway gateway clusters. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit crafted API calls to web management endpoints, bypassing authentication handlers to execute arbitrary commands under system privileges. Cisco issued software update release X15.5.20, confirming that legacy software streams including X14 or earlier must be migrated immediately.
Subverting edge collaboration appliances compromises perimeter network boundaries and enterprise communication security. Because Cisco Expressway manages secure external SIP calling, remote workforce connectivity, and video conferencing traversal, an unauthenticated gateway takeover permits threat actors to intercept internal communications, drop persistent remote access implants, and pivot into corporate subnets.
- Upgrade Cisco Expressway Series appliances immediately to fixed software release version X15.5.20. - Restrict public internet exposure of Expressway administrative web interfaces, enforcing access through dedicated management VLANs. - Inspect system process trees and network connections on Expressway nodes for unauthorized shell execution or unexpected egress channels. - Invalidate active administrative session cookies and force credential rotations across all managed collaboration appliances.
Edge collaboration security requires rapid software patch deployment and out-of-band management isolation to ensure perimeter communication gateways remain insulated from unauthenticated remote code execution. #CodeDefence #Cisco #Expressway #CVE202676466 #ZeroDay #RCE #PerimeterSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CISA

item.title: Critical NGINX2Root vulnerabilities CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 allow unauthenticated server takeover
item.description:
Web server threat intelligence reports published today warn of dual critical vulnerabilities affecting high-performance web proxy infrastructure. Remote unauthenticated threat actors exploit HTTP/2 request frame parsing bugs to trigger memory corruption and achieve full root control over vulnerable web servers.
The vulnerability disclosures, dubbed NGINX2Root and tracked as CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, carry CVSS scores up to 9.8 and impact NGINX open-source and NGINX Plus web servers running active HTTP/2 modules. Unauthenticated remote adversaries send malformed HTTP/2 stream frames to trigger heap buffer overflows in worker process memory. Technical proof-of-concept writeups demonstrate chaining these NGINX memory bugs with local Linux kernel privilege escalation flaws to escalate initial web daemon access to full root execution. Censys exposure telemetry indicates over 8.8 million exposed services globally.
Subverting central web servers and reverse proxies poses severe systemic risks to enterprise application hosting environments. Because NGINX acts as the primary ingress controller and SSL TLS termination endpoint for millions of web applications, an unauthenticated remote root takeover allows threat actors to hijack traffic, steal session tokens, and compromise backend database networks.
- Apply official NGINX security patches immediately across all web server fleets and container ingress controllers. - Disable HTTP/2 protocol support temporarily on exposed listeners if immediate patching cannot be executed across legacy hosts. - Enforce strict Web Application Firewall WAF rules to inspect and drop malformed HTTP/2 framing requests at the edge. - Audit Linux host kernel versions and execute immediate privilege escalation hardening to block local root escalation chains.
Web ingress defense demands immediate software patch application and strict protocol inspection to ensure enterprise reverse proxies remain protected against unauthenticated memory corruption exploits. #CodeDefence #NGINX #NGINX2Root #CVE2026123007 #CVE2026123633 #HTTP2 #RCE #WebSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #CloudSecurity
